Mutation check: I removed the early integrity short-circuit in presence::ensure. The test then failed with "an unchanged lock runs nothing, left: 4 right: 3". I restored the code before the final run.
findings_addressed: B1 reviewer deviation 6 ('Nothing builds venvs/presence yet'): the `111 install` stage step now builds it. `stage::presence_venv` runs on both the fresh path and the 'already staged' path, but only when the manifest pins [presence-lock]. It uses the lock inside the release tree, which verify_layer5_tree has already checked against the pin (B1's call sites are unchanged).

Same pattern as the rns venv: `pip install --require-hashes` from a cache with `--no-index`, plus the `.111-integrity` marker holding the lock's sha256. At install the closure is downloaded into the root-owned cache/packages/presence/. After install, rebuilds use that cache only, so nothing downloads at runtime.

Rebuild after a promotion: `venv::presence::ensure_current(layout, runner)` compares the venv with the lock in current/. The same lock runs nothing (Outcome::Unchanged, zero tool calls, no file writes). A changed lock rebuilds offline and prunes older builds.

Fail closed: each build goes into a new dir venvs/presence.d/<sha16>-<pid>-<n>. venvs/presence is a link that is swapped by tmp link + rename only after pip succeeded, bin/python exists and the marker is written. A hash mismatch, a missing wheel, a venv failure or no python3 removes the unfinished build and leaves the old venv untouched (Outcome::Unavailable { previous_kept }). Typed PresenceVenvError; no panics.
The reader_python path stays venvs/presence/bin/python, now reached through the link. A test asserts it equals MeshtasticConfig::production(..).reader_python and is a file.

Reason: there was no venv reason on the meshtastic row. The M1 bounce's python3 visibility only covers the skip message in the api_v1_meshtastic tests. Every ensure now writes venvs/presence.status.json with code presence_venv_ready, presence_no_python or presence_venv_failed, plus a plain-language reason that says whether the old venv stays in use. In meshtastic/mod.rs, spawn_reader's log line now prints that reason; the old default text is kept when no status exists. Putting it on the service row needs services/mod.rs (deviation 2).

Safety when the root installer writes into the node111-owned venvs/: links at venvs/ and venvs/presence.d are refused, not followed (tested: nothing is written through a planted link). The flock lock file and the status reader use O_NOFOLLOW. Pruning removes a link itself, never what it points to. A hand-made real venvs/presence directory is moved aside and replaced (tested), and put back if the swap fails. A crash between creating the tmp link and the rename leaves a link that the next build sweeps.

Tests use a fake python3/pip made of real shell scripts run by SystemRunner (tests/fake_python/mod.rs). They cover: a fresh full install (run_with) builds the venv before step 7 chowns venvs/ (call order asserted); an install re-run leaves it alone; an install never fails on a hash mismatch, a failed download or missing python3, and the next run builds it once fixed; an update staged by the real updater (check_once with a [presence-lock] pin), then promoted, rebuilds; an unchanged lock does nothing; a pip failure keeps the old venv; no python3 keeps the old venv; a revert clears the reason; a release without the reader is NotShipped and runs nothing.
rns behaviour is unchanged: same functions, same commands, same error strings. I only factored out marker_is() and offline_install_args(). tests/transport_venv.rs passes unmodified.
10-bootstrap/README.md Layer 5 State line now describes venvs/presence, presence.d/, cache/packages/presence/, the status file and the fail-closed rule.
gaps: Nothing in production calls ensure_current yet, so a promoted update whose lock changed is not rebuilt until the daemon start calls it. The rns venv is not rebuilt at promotion either: transport::start runs venv::ensure at daemon start from src/daemon/mod.rs, and the root helper only flips current and restarts the service. So update_helper.rs was correctly left alone, and the daemon-start call belongs in src/daemon/mod.rs, which I don't own (deviation 1). Suspected owner: lead or the daemon/mod.rs owner.

The meshtastic service row still says node_db_pending ('waiting for the board's list of nodes') forever when meshmud runs but the reader has no venv. The reason is in venvs/presence.status.json and in the daemon log, but not in the row's reason. That needs services/mod.rs (MeshmudFacts field + rule) and a facts() fill in meshtastic/mod.rs beyond the reason string (deviation 2). Owner: the services/meshtastic owner (M1 line).

After install, nothing fetches the wheels for a changed lock. The offline rebuild after promotion only works if cache/packages/presence already holds the new closure. Otherwise it fails closed, keeps the old venv, and the reason tells the user to run `111 install` again. rns has the same gap and worse: cache/packages/python/rns-lock.txt is written only by `111 install`, so an update that changes rns-lock never takes effect. Owner question: ship the wheels in the payload, have the updater or helper prefetch them, or require an install re-run.

Existing rns gap, found while reading: packages_for(Debian) installs python3 + python3-venv but not python3-pip. So packages::pip_closure's `python3 -m pip --version` fails on a fresh Debian/Ubuntu, the rns closure is never prefetched, and the daemon's offline rns build fails, leaving the node with no transport. Confirmed on this box: `/usr/bin/python3: No module named pip`. The presence path avoids this by downloading with the build venv's own pip. Owner: bootstrap (rns parts of packages.rs, outside my presence-only ownership).
No receipt degrade branch for a failed presence venv at install. stage::run cannot reach the receipt; the status file is the record. Optional deviation 3.

Not exercised against real pip/PyPI or a real meshtastic closure; tests use the fake tools. The symlinked-prefix venv layout was probed by hand with a real `python3 -m venv --without-pip` (Python 3.10.12): sys.prefix and site-packages resolve through the link. A Termux/phone run of the presence venv remains an external gate.
deviations: 2 (services/mod.rs + meshtastic/mod.rs facts(), beyond 'the reason string only'). Add `pub reader_unavailable: Option<String>` to MeshmudFacts. In Meshtastic::facts(), fill it with `(!cfg.reader_installed()).then(|| venv::presence::unavailable_reason(&cfg.root).unwrap_or_else(|| "The presence reader is not installed on this node.".into()))`, cached in refresh() like the other facts. In services::meshtastic(), add an arm before `ChildDisplay::Running if !m.node_db_present`: `ChildDisplay::Running if !m.node_db_present && m.reader_unavailable.is_some()` → ServiceState::Error, code "presence_unavailable", reason = that string. Also add `"reader_unavailable"` to detail. Optionally also expose the stale case (previous_kept) in detail.

3 (install/mod.rs, optional). Push `receipt.degrade_branches` when stage::presence_venv returns Outcome::Unavailable. stage::presence_venv is pub and returns the outcome, so the call would be a small refactor of step 6.

Departures from the rns pattern, needed for fail-closed and robustness: (a) venvs/presence is a link to a complete build under venvs/presence.d/, not a dir rebuilt in place (rns deletes first, which cannot keep the previous venv); (b) the install-time download uses the build venv's own pip, not host `python3 -m pip`, which is absent on Debian/Ubuntu by default; (c) a status file venvs/presence.status.json; (d) an flock serialising installer and daemon builds.

The 'fake pip/python3 on PATH' tests resolve python3 through a test Runner (tests/fake_python/mod.rs, a new file under tests/) instead of changing the process PATH. That avoids races with the other tests that share the environment; the fakes are still real executables run by SystemRunner.

update_helper.rs untouched (the rns venv rebuild does not live there). guard.rs, api_v1_panels.rs and docs/release-checklist.md in the dirty tree belong to the parallel agent. My test run compiled them and was green at that moment.
result.notes:
Where to look:
(1) venv.rs `presence` module: ensure() checks integrity first, so an unchanged lock runs zero commands. It re-checks under the flock, and only build_and_swap touches the venv in place, via one rename in flip(). After a fresh-dir build, the venv's bin/pip shebang points at presence.d/<id>/bin/python, which is correct because the build stays at that path. The reader's bin/python works through the link (checked by hand with real Python 3.10.12).
(2) An `Unchanged` status write happens only if the recorded status differs, e.g. after a revert. The test asserts the status bytes are identical across an unchanged promotion.
(3) Reason texts (in the status file, so user-visible once deviation 2 lands): previous venv kept → "The presence reader's environment for this release could not be built (…), so the reader runs on the one built earlier."; none → "The presence reader is off: its environment could not be built (…)."; the offline pip failure adds "running `111 install` again downloads them". The quoted tool output is the first ERROR: line, or else the last line, with control characters stripped, capped at 200 bytes.
(4) Residual TOCTOU: a compromised node111 could swap venvs/presence.d for a link between the installer's lstat and its use. The installer already chowns and writes into node111 trees as root, so I judged checks plus O_NOFOLLOW proportionate. Worth a look in fable review.
(5) I applied rustfmt to my files only (not crate-wide `cargo fmt`), to avoid reformatting the parallel agent's in-progress files. The crate-wide `cargo fmt --check` was green anyway.
(6) Never committed. The target dir is target-VENV under the scratchpad; all cargo runs used CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=6, one at a time.
